key_insight: LEAP combines a domain-specialized LLM with active learning to prioritize perovskite precursor additives in a closed loop, making additive discovery more mechanism-aware and data-efficient.
engineering_relevance: For solar-cell engineering, the framework can reduce experimental screening effort while improving the odds of finding additives that boost device efficiency under low-data conditions.
method: LLM extracts mechanism-relevant knowledge from perovskite additive literature.
Molecules are encoded with interpretable descriptors and fed into Bayesian optimization for uncertainty-aware ranking.
Experts review feasibility and guide iterative screening across rounds.
evidence_signal: On unseen literature, the domain-specialized model outperformed general-purpose models, and the proof-of-concept screening achieved average PCEs of 20.13% and 20.87% in later rounds versus 19.25% for control, with a 21.32% champion device.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of literature-derived descriptors plus expert feasibility review, so transfer to new chemistries may be limited by data and bias.
paper_title: LEAP: A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery
